It raised On-Time Delivery Rate by 3.1 pts but cut checkout conversion by 1.2%, and the gain came from relaxed promises, not faster delivery. The proposal does not mention this experiment or explain how it differs.","evidence_quote":"Give customers a more generous arrival range by adding 10 extra minutes of cushion in the three worst zones, to lift on-time rate.","citations":["experiment-registry#exp-014-eta-buffer"],"recommendation":"Cite EXP-014, explain what is different this time (for example, zone targeting), and state why conversion is not expected to drop again. Otherwise do not rerun the test."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"No checkout conversion guardrail for a promise-window change","detail":"EXP-014 learned that promise changes must be judged on Promise Accuracy and conversion, not on OTD alone. The proposal includes Promise Accuracy but has no conversion guardrail, even though the prior test lost 1.2% conversion.","evidence_quote":"","citations":["experiment-registry#exp-014-eta-buffer"],"recommendation":"Add checkout conversion as a guardrail with a numeric stop threshold, and judge success on Promise Accuracy and conversion together with On-Time Delivery Rate."}]}
